details.description: A production payment token is hardcoded in source code which can be leaked via source control or deployed artifacts.
details.fix_explanation: Move secrets into environment variables or a secret store. Read PAYMENT_TOKEN via os.getenv and fail safely if not set.

details.description: Mail server credentials are hardcoded and can be leaked.
details.fix_explanation: Use environment variables or vault to hold mail server keys, load with os.getenv.

details.vulnerability_type: Hardcoded internal secret (INTERNAL_AUTH) and weak use of it
details.description: INTERNAL_AUTH is hardcoded and is used with MD5 to derive tokens — both practices are insecure.
details.fix_explanation: Store INTERNAL_AUTH in environment; use a secure HMAC-SHA256 for token generation instead of MD5-based concatenation.
details.secure_code_snippet:
INTERNAL_AUTH = os.getenv("INTERNAL_AUTH")
# generate tokens with HMAC-SHA256
token = hmac.new(INTERNAL_AUTH.encode(), username.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()

details.description: The query uses string interpolation to place the uid into the SQL statement which allows SQL injection.
details.fix_explanation: Use parameterized queries (placeholders) provided by sqlite3 to ensure values are bound rather than interpolated into SQL.
details.secure_code_snippet: c.execute("SELECT id, name, balance FROM profiles WHERE id = ?", (uid,))

details.vulnerability_type: SSRF and token disclosure via external notify_url
details.description: The code posts sensitive PAYMENT_TOKEN to an arbitrary notify_url supplied by the requester which allows token leakage and SSRF attacks.
details.fix_explanation: Validate notify_url hostnames against a whitelist; do not include internal secrets in outbound requests. Use a secure service-to-service auth mechanism if needed.

details.description: update_records opens an arbitrary path passed by the user, enabling reading sensitive files or path traversal.
details.fix_explanation: Limit file access to a safe config directory, check file extension and ensure the resolved path starts with the safe base directory.
details.secure_code_snippet:
file_path = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(CONFIG_DIR, relative_path))
if not file_path.startswith(CONFIG_DIR): raise PermissionError('access denied')

details.description: export_data builds a shell command using user-supplied data and executes it with shell=True which allows command injection.
details.fix_explanation: Avoid shell execution entirely; use Python's zipfile module or subprocess with argument list (no shell) and validate filenames.
details.secure_code_snippet:
with zipfile.ZipFile(outname, 'w', zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
    zf.write(DB_FILE, arcname=os.path.basename(DB_FILE))

details.description: Endpoints that affect data or trigger external actions (transfer, config, export) have no authentication, allowing unauthenticated abuse.
details.fix_explanation: Require a valid admin API token in request headers for sensitive endpoints (e.g., X-ADMIN-TOKEN) and validate server side.

details.description: The code prints transaction details to stdout which can leak sensitive information in logs.
details.fix_explanation: Use structured logging and avoid printing sensitive fields. Mask or redact sensitive values before logging.

details.description: Running Flask in debug mode exposes debugger and code execution in production, leaking internals and enabling RCE.
details.fix_explanation: Never run Flask with debug=True in production; configure environment for development only and use debug False in production.
